title: Drones Sink Ships Near NATO Countries, EU Calls Attacks 'Unacceptable'
title_zh: 无人机击沉北约国家附近船只，欧盟称袭击“不可接受”
lead: For the first time, drones have sunk cargo ships inside the waters of NATO member countries. At least two sailors were killed, and the European Union has described the attacks as unacceptable.

paragraphs: Two cargo ships were sunk and a third was set on fire by drones in the exclusive economic zones of NATO countries, killing at least two sailors. The Togo-flagged ship Alfa Watan sank, and the Palau-flagged ship Able caught fire after being attacked by sea and aerial drones about 80 miles off Bulgaria's coast on October 6. Bulgaria's Prime Minister called it 'an unacceptable attack' and 'a blatant violation of international law.'

The Able's 18 crew members were rescued by a Bulgarian ferry, and two injured sailors were flown to a hospital in Varna. The Alfa Watan's crew fate was unknown. This followed an attack one day earlier on the Turkish-owned ship Royad Mammadov inside Romania's exclusive economic zone; that ship caught fire and sank, with 11 rescued, two killed and one missing.

EU President Ursula von der Leyen said the strikes were 'increasingly concerning' but noted the circumstances were still being established. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, however, said a joint investigation with Bulgaria found it was a 'Russian combined attack.' He denied Ukraine was operating in that part of the Black Sea.

The attacks show how the war has widened since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has used drones to challenge Russian naval power, and Russia has increasingly targeted international cargo ships carrying grain. The Able was carrying wheat when it was hit.

The strikes come as several European countries report incidents of Russian hybrid warfare. Romania has destroyed Russian drones near a gas project, Germany accused Russia of a drone attack plot at Leipzig Airport, and Poland is investigating a fire at a satellite station as sabotage.
paragraphs_zh: 两艘货船被无人机击沉，第三艘起火，事发地点位于北约国家的专属经济区内，造成至少两名水手死亡。悬挂多哥国旗的“Alfa Watan”号沉没，悬挂帕劳国旗的“Able”号在10月6日于保加利亚海岸约80英里处遭海上和空中无人机袭击后起火。保加利亚总理称这是“不可接受的袭击”和“对国际法和海洋法的公然违反”。
“Able”号的18名船员被一艘保加利亚渡轮救起，两名受伤水手被送往瓦尔纳的医院。“Alfa Watan”号船员的命运尚不清楚。此前一天，土耳其拥有的“Royad Mammadov”号在罗马尼亚专属经济区内遭到袭击；该船起火并沉没，11人获救，2人死亡，1人失踪。
欧盟主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩表示这些袭击“越来越令人担忧”，但指出事件情况仍在调查中。然而，乌克兰总统泽连斯基称，与保加利亚的联合调查发现这是一次“俄罗斯的联合攻击”。他否认乌克兰在该黑海区域开展行动。
这些袭击表明，自2022年俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来，战争范围已经扩大。乌克兰利用无人机挑战俄罗斯的海上力量，而俄罗斯则越来越多地针对运载谷物的国际货船。“Able”号被击中时正运载小麦。
此次袭击发生之际，多个欧洲国家报告了俄罗斯混合战事件。罗马尼亚在天然气项目附近摧毁了俄罗斯无人机，德国指责俄罗斯策划在莱比锡机场发动无人机袭击，波兰正在将卫星站火灾作为破坏活动进行调查。

Drones sank two cargo ships and damaged a third in the exclusive economic zones of NATO member countries for the first time, killing at least two sailors. The attacks represent a notable escalation as Black Sea commercial shipping has increasingly come under attack during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, with Russia also being accused of carrying out “hybrid warfare” incidents across Europe.
The Togo-flagged cargo ship
Alfa Watan
sank, and the Palau-flagged cargo ship
Able
was set ablaze after being attacked by multiple sea and aerial drones about 80 miles (128 kilometers) off the coast of Bulgaria on October 6,
according to the Associated Press
. In an interview, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev described the incidents as “an unacceptable attack in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone” and “a blatant violation of international law and maritime law.”
The fate of the
Alfa Watan’
s crew was not immediately known after the vessel sank. A Bulgarian ferry managed to evacuate the 18 crew members of the
Able
, with two severely injured mariners being flown to a hospital in the city of Varna.
This comes one day after drones struck the Turkish-owned cargo ship named
Royad Mammadov
within Romania’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea on October 5. That ship caught fire and eventually sank, with 11 crew members rescued by Romanian ships and helicopters while one crew member remains missing,
according to Euronews
. Two crew members were killed.
European Union president Ursula von der Leyen described the drone strikes on the three vessels in the Black Sea as “increasingly concerning” in a
post on X
. But she also cautioned that the circumstances of the attacks are “still being established” without naming a probable attacker.
“Attacks on civilian shipping are unacceptable,” Leyen wrote. “We stand in full solidarity with our Member States on the Eastern flank.”
By contrast, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described a joint investigation with Bulgaria’s navy as finding that the latest strikes represented a “Russian combined attack using both sea and aerial drones,”
Reuters reported
. Zelenskyy also said that Ukraine’s military was not conducting operations in that part of the Black Sea.
Widening Black Sea warfare
The attacks represent the widening consequences of the ongoing war that escalated sharply with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Despite lacking much of a traditional navy, Ukraine has successfully challenged Russian naval control of the Black Sea by deploying both aerial drones and drone boats to strike Russian warships and ports.
Ukrainian drones have also stepped up
attacks on Russian-linked oil and gas tankers along with other supply ships
. In a milestone for naval warfare, a
Ukrainian sea drone even used a machine gun to sink a Russian kamikaze drone boat
carrying explosives in September 2026.
But Russia has also increasingly deployed its own aerial drones and sea drones to attack Ukrainian ships and ports, along with
attacking international commercial ships
carrying
grain and other cargo from Ukraine
or docked in Ukrainian ports.
The cargo ship
Able
was carrying wheat and sailing south when the drones attacked, while the
Alfa Watan
was heading north with the cargo being unknown. The
Royad Mammadov
had been carrying corn loaded in the Ukrainian port of Ismail when it was reportedly attacked by both aerial drones and drone boats.
In a
social media post
reacting to the earlier attack on the
Royad Mammadov
, Zelenskyy condemned the “horrific strike by two Russian drones on a civilian vessel in neutral waters” and reiterated Ukrainian efforts to “de-escalate the situation and ensure security in the Black Sea.”
“But Russia consistently chooses terror and sinking civilian vessels instead of normal maritime navigation,” Zelenskyy wrote. “Pressure is needed to restore global food security.”
Zelenskyy also referred to “relevant proposals from third countries” on this topic. India has been holding discussions with both Ukraine and Russia on safeguarding shipping in the Black Sea and has generally called for a halt to the fighting,
according to Bloomberg News
.
India has a strategic partnership with Russia that includes the Indian military using Russian fighter jets and air defense systems, while the country continues to purchase Russian oil for its energy needs. But many Indian citizens also work as seafarers on commercial vessels that have come under attack in the Black Sea and Strait of Hormuz, with three Indian nationals having been aboard the
Royad Mammadov
and one
being injured in the attack
.
Hybrid warfare in Europe
The latest drone strikes on ships off the coasts of Romania and Bulgaria coincide with a growing number of incidents attributed to Russian hybrid warfare or gray-zone tactics aimed at multiple European countries within the NATO alliance.
Russian embassy officials have denied this
, but the evidence continues to accumulate, with multiple European governments pointing to Russia.
For example, Romanian military divers previously
destroyed two Russian-made drones found floating in the Black Sea
near the vital European natural gas project called Neptun Deep in August. A few weeks later, Romania
scrambled fighter jets to disable a Russian drone boat
loaded with explosives that was also discovered near the same offshore gas platform.
Germany has also
formally accused Russia
of organizing an
attempted explosive drone attack on Ukrainian cargo aircraft
parked at Leipzig Airport in August. Meanwhile, Estonia has also described Russian special services as being behind an
arson attack on the Estonian company Milrem Robotics
, which supplies Ukraine with
military robotic vehicles
.
Similarly, Poland has been investigating a fire at a state-owned satellite station using SpaceX’s
Starlink communication service
as an “act of sabotage” that aligns with a “new Russian doctrine of attack,” according to Polish Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski as
reported by BBC News
.
Much of the NATO alliance is still rearming and trying to
adapt to modern warfare dominated by drones
, which both
Ukraine and Russia have already spent years developing and practicing on the battlefield
. But the Russian-instigated hybrid warfare across Europe poses a different immediate challenge—can NATO member countries agree on a strategy for discouraging sabotage and other provocative incidents from a nuclear-armed adversary?

Jeremy Hsu is a reporter exploring a wide range of topics across deep tech and AI. He has previously written for New Scientist, Scientific American, IEEE Spectrum, Wired, Undark Magazine and MIT Tech Review, among many other publications, about topics such as deepfakes, data centers, drones, battery tech, robotics, and GPS jamming.
